title: 40,000 starlings flocking live in the browser, a 3D murmuration made with LittleJS
author: Slackluster
selftext:
I made a starling murmuration in 3D with LittleJS, built by iterating with Claude.

All 40,000 birds are simulated live using grid-based boids flocking. Move your mouse to steer a hawk through the flock and watch it scatter. The lake reflects everything with real waves, and the mountains, sky and water are generated in code, with no image files.

Press G to send the flock streaming off over the mountains, and F to fly the camera around.

Try it: [https://killedbyapixel.github.io/LittleJS-Demos/murmuration/](https://killedbyapixel.github.io/LittleJS-Demos/murmuration/)

LittleJS, the engine: [https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body:
Hey u/Slackluster, this falls under Rule 4. Sharing your game is okay here, free or paid, but you need to talk about how it was developed using AI, so the community has something to discuss. This post doesn't have enough on that yet.

To keep it up, edit your post or reply to this comment within an hour with some details on your dev process, like:

- which AI tools you used, and what for
- how they fit into your workflow
- problems you hit and how you dealt with them

"Made with AI", a list of tools or a ChatGPT bullet list won't cut it. If nothing's added by then, this post may be removed.

If you think we got this wrong, [message the mods](https://www.reddit.com/message/compose?to=/r/aigamedev).

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
Sure! I used Claude Code for pretty much all of it, the flocking, the 3D scene, the water shader, even rendering the video. It's built on LittleJS, my engine, so I could tell when it was doing things right.

My workflow was mostly playing it and telling Claude what felt off. Stuff like "the hawk disappears before it gets off screen" or "the mountains all scoop down where the sun is, it looks kind of fake." Then it would dig in, fix it, and I'd check again.

Some problems we hit: the starlings were flickering in the water reflection because they were smaller than a pixel in it, so Claude just took them out of the reflection. At the end the flock was flying away in two groups, and I wanted it more like a stream of bats. That was coming from two attractor points pulling the flock apart, so it merged them into one exit point.

Biggest thing I learned is to just describe what looks wrong, not how to fix it. Claude was pretty good at finding the actual cause.

Demo: [https://killedbyapixel.github.io/LittleJS-Demos/murmuration/](https://killedbyapixel.github.io/LittleJS-Demos/murmuration/)
